summary.headline: Neuland Q2 FY27 revenue fell to Rs457.2 Cr (from Rs516.1 Cr) and EBITDA margin to 22.9%, with management blaming commercial shipment lumpiness.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was Rs457.2 Cr versus Rs516.1 Cr a year ago, while H1 FY27 income rose to Rs1,107.2 Cr from Rs816.7 Cr. EBITDA was Rs104.6 Cr (22.9% margin) against Rs156.9 Cr (30.4%) and PAT fell to Rs51.1 Cr from Rs96.5 Cr. Management described the quarter as below recent trend but said H1 was broadly in line with its expectations. Working capital rose to 104 days from 84 days, and the company reiterated that FY27 and FY28 will grow without giving numeric guidance.

segments.name: CMS (commercial molecules)
segments.commentary: Drove most of Q2 revenue; management cited Rs214 Cr of CMS revenue in Q2 per analyst question, with roughly 5-6 commercial molecules contributing. No new launches in the last 2-3 quarters; last launch about a year ago.

segments.name: GDS (prime and specialty portfolios)
segments.commentary: Specialty segment was muted YoY and QoQ because customers of a few key specialty molecules had manufacturing difficulties; management expects normalisation by Q4 FY27. Filed 2 DMFs (Fezolinetant and Ivacaftor) in the period.

guidance_outlook: No numeric growth guidance; management said FY27 and FY28 will both grow, but declined to give a range.
Capex guidance for the next three years was indicated at roughly Rs1,700-1,800 Cr; management said this number is revisited, with Kakinada affecting it.
Peptide Module 1 has cost about Rs250 Cr so far; Module 2 configuration to be finalised in the next 3-6 months.
Peptide PPQ-related revenue expected in 6-9 months; commercial peptide revenue roughly 1.5-2 years out.
No expiries of key molecules expected before 2030; management says business will grow despite post-2030 declines.
Management expects some headcount additions for R&D and peptide/API manufacturing.
capex_capacity: Peptide Module 1 commissioned at Unit I with encouraging traction; Modules 2-4 to be configured as project visibility emerges. Module 1 uses DAC columns sized for current projects, with SPPS and LPPS reactors. Largest GMP SPPS reactor moved from 50 L to 500 L, with 1,000 L planned.
Acquired about 134 acres at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh; right of first refusal on about 60 more acres, with a possible total of about 200 acres over two years. Management urged a long-term return view.
Board approved buying additional land to expand Unit I footprint.
New process R&D centre at Genome Valley, Hyderabad, expected fully operational by early next year; focused on small molecules and peptides, not new modalities such as oligos, ADCs or HPAPIs for now.
Kakinada spending may be slowed if commercial molecules are hit, while peptide Modules 2-4 would proceed regardless.
demand_pricing: RFP activity in FY27 is the strongest to date, per management, with several opportunities from long-standing relationships.
Diversifying the customer base; progress with big pharma, though several new proposals come from newer customers. Top 5 customers were cited at 68% of revenue.
Input costs rose in H1 due to geopolitical conflicts causing raw material volatility and higher freight and logistics costs.
Management sees peptide demand rising, with about 1,000 synthetic peptides between IND and commercial stages versus about 500 in January 2025; expects some overcapacity risk in China but not India.
On AI-driven discovery, management sees it as a tailwind for IND-onwards development and manufacturing, but has no concrete evidence yet that RFP growth is AI-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Who bears the cost if the peptide plant sits idle for about three years, and what do contracts say?
qa_highlights.answer: Peptide work starts with MSAs for PPQ batches, then moves to commercial supply agreements. Idle capacity cost is generally not passed to customers unless the plant is built for a specific project, so Neuland expects to bear idle costs for 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: When will peptide revenue be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: PPQ-related peptide revenue is expected in 6-9 months; the first PPQ batches may ship in that window. Commercial revenue follows after a further 6-9 months, which management agreed is a reasonable 1.5-2 year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a launch or large order in prior quarters that has not recurred?
qa_highlights.answer: No launches in the last 2-3 quarters. Variation reflects lumpy commercial shipments; management does not disclose molecule-level data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is specialty segment muted YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: A few specialty molecules that contributed significantly have been hit by customers' manufacturing difficulties. Management expects normalisation by Q4 based on customer feedback.

qa_highlights.question: Why are revenue and profit lumpy, and will this ease?
qa_highlights.answer: A handful of molecules drive commercial revenue and orders are irregular. Lumpiness should reduce only if the number of large contributors rises substantially; management does not expect it to end within 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the view on peptide overcapacity and talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes there is no overcapacity in India, that China may be overcapacity, and that India lacks talent for peptide CDMO work, though it has talent for generics.

risks_watch: Lumpy commercial shipments and no visible launches for 2-3 quarters make quarterly revenue and margin hard to forecast.
Concentration risk: top 5 customers at 68% of revenue.
Peptide Modules 2-4 and Kakinada add capex; Module 1 may sit underused for 1-1.5 years, borne by Neuland.
Raw material and freight cost pressure in H2 FY27.
Working capital days up to 104 from 84 QoQ.
Watch specialty segment recovery by Q4 FY27 and PPQ revenue from peptides in 6-9 months.
Module 2 configuration and updated capex guidance expected in the next 3-6 months.
summary.management_tone: Candid and defensive on the quarter, attributing the drop to lumpiness and specialty customer issues. Confident on long-term pipeline, peptides and Kakinada, but reticent on numeric guidance and molecule-level detail.
key_quotes: As the numbers show this quarter has been below the trend that we have seen over the last few quarters; however, if we consider the first half of the year it was largely consistent with our expectations.
There has been no launch in the last two, three quarters.
I would probably urge investors to look at the investment in Kakinada more from a long-term return perspective rather than something that will give us returns in the immediate timeframe.
I think 2027 will grow and then 2028 will also grow, but yes, I do not think we are precise enough to go into more clarity there.

growth.why: Management said FY27 and FY28 will both grow but gave no numeric range; Q2 revenue fell about 11% YoY and EBITDA about 33% on specialty customer manufacturing issues, with peptide capacity (Module 1 live, Modules 2-4 unconfirmed) and Kakinada deferred, so backing is vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 22.9% from 30.4% YoY and gross margin slipped to 59.4% from 60.1%, with raw material and freight cost pressure flagged for H2 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Peptide Module 1 is already commissioned at Unit I (Rs250 Cr spent), with Module 2 configuration to be finalised in 3-6 months, but Modules 2-4 are conditional on project visibility and Kakinada is deferred.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says FY27 and FY28 will both grow with no numeric range, RFP activity is the strongest to date, and specialty normalisation is expected by Q4 FY27, but Q2 revenue fell about 11% YoY (Rs457.2 Cr vs Rs516.1 Cr).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Module 2 configuration and updated capex guidance (currently Rs1,700-1,800 Cr over three years, under revisit) are due in 3-6 months, and the board has approved additional land at Unit I.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was given, and Q2 total income fell about 11% YoY with EBITDA down about 33%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Specialty customers' manufacturing issues, lumpy commercial shipments with no launches for 2-3 quarters, and working capital up to 104 days from 84 could push results below trend.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new molecule launches in the last 2-3 quarters (last about a year ago), and commercial peptide revenue is 1.5-2 years out; PPQ-related peptide revenue is expected in 6-9 months.

rows.label: Peptide PPQ revenue ramp
rows.why: PPQ-related peptide revenue expected in 6-9 months and the first PPQ batches may ship in that window, though commercial peptide revenue is 1.5-2 years out.

rows.label: Specialty segment recovery
rows.why: Management expects normalisation of specialty molecules hit by customers' manufacturing difficulties by Q4 FY27, based on customer feedback.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation
rows.why: Working capital days rose to 104 from 84 QoQ, and the reason for reversal is not stated in the brief.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term pipeline, peptides, and Kakinada and attributed the drop to lumpy commercial shipments and specialty customer issues, but gave no numeric guidance or molecule-level detail; analysts pushed on the idle cost of Module 1, peptide revenue timing, and the reasons
